# Tim's Furniture Repair

> Furniture repair based in Bloomington, Indiana. Furniture repair from Tim's woodshop on Bloomington's east side. Wobbly chairs reglued tight, broken legs and bases rebuilt, rockers and antique cane chairs put right, wood stained to match. Fast work at a fair price.

- Phone: (812) 327-6392
- Based in: Bloomington, IN
- Service area: Bloomington, Ellettsville, Nashville, Bedford, Spencer, Martinsville
- Google rating: 4.6 from 10 reviews

- Book a visit: https://ronaks-code.github.io/sitelift-demos/upholstery/indiana/tim-s-furniture-repair/book.html

## Services
- Broken legs, frames & bases: Legs snapped in a move, cracked frames and split bases repaired or rebuilt to match the original design.
- Chair regluing & tightening: Wobbly dining and kitchen chairs taken apart, cleaned up and clamped back together with strong glue so they stop rocking.
- Antique & cane-back chairs: Older chairs with cane seats and backs brought back into shape, with loose joints and worn wood repaired.
- Rockers & recliners: Broken wooden parts on rocking chairs and recliners repaired so they rock and sit right again.
- Custom woodwork & new parts: New parts made to fit, from crossbeams to whole bases, duplicating the original design. Tim customizes pieces too.
- Staining, wheels & casters: New wood stained to blend in, and replacement wheels and casters found close to the originals.

## About
Tim's Furniture Repair is Tim's woodshop on the east side of Bloomington, out on State Road 46 Bypass. Look for the blue sign with the dragons at the driveway. Tim does every repair himself, and fixing furniture so people can keep enjoying it is the part he loves. Most of what comes through the door is chairs: dining and kitchen chairs that have gone wobbly, a wing-back with a leg snapped in a move, a recliner with broken wooden parts, antique cane-back chairs, rolling barrel chairs that sat in a barn for 15 years. Tim takes them apart, rebuilds what's broken to the original design, finds wheels that match and stains new wood so it blends in. The shop itself is a comeback story. A plaque by the door thanks the local businesses and trades who helped get the wood shop back in business, from the concrete crew to the electricians and the tree service. Customers keep saying the same three things: he's quick, the work holds up, and the price is fair, sometimes even less than he first quoted. Plenty of them come back with the next piece.

## Frequently asked questions
- Q: What kind of furniture do you repair?
  A: All kinds of furniture, loose or broken: dining and kitchen chairs, broken wooden legs, rockers and recliners, antique cane-back chairs, table and chair bases, and worn casters. Not sure about yours? Call (812) 327-6392.
- Q: Can you fix a wobbly chair?
  A: Yes. Tim takes wobbly chairs apart and puts them back together with a strong glue. Customers say their chairs no longer wobble.
- Q: Do you fix rocking chairs and recliners?
  A: Yes. Tim has repaired the broken wooden parts of recliners and rockers. A customer called the job excellent, fast and professional.
- Q: Can you match the original wood and wheels?
  A: Yes. Tim has rebuilt chair bases to duplicate the original design, found replacement wheels very close to the originals and stained the wood to match.
- Q: Do you do fabric or cushion work?
  A: The reviews are about frames, legs, joints and bases. For fabric or cushion work, call (812) 327-6392 and ask.
- Q: Where is the shop? Do I need an appointment?
  A: 5921 E State Rd 46 Bypass, on Bloomington's east side, at the blue sign. Tim works by appointment, so call (812) 327-6392 first.
